name: Tepo Krumen
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Thalmann, Peter. 1980. Phonologie du kroumen. 65pp (SIL/ILA Abidjan); also Thalmann 1987 Elements de grammaire Kroumen Tepo (494pp). Neither online; SIL blocked.

new_statements.quote: Le kroumen tépo est une langue à trois niveaux tonals comportant les tons H, M et Ba et Bb, ainsi que la séquence BH - en fait BbH -, qui se réalise comme un ton modulé bas montant. Ainsi, une syllabe est susceptible de comporter l'une de ces quatre mélodies H, M, B (>Ba et Bb), BbH. [...] A part les unités phonématiques et la nasalisation, ce sont aussi les tons qui servent à différencier les signifiants kroumen tépo. Chaque syllabe d'un lexème monomonématique est caractérisée par l'une des quatre mélodies suivantes : haut (H), moyen (M), bas (B), bas montant (BH)
new_statements.translation: Tepo Krumen is a language with three tone levels comprising the tones H, M and Ba and Bb, as well as the sequence BH - in fact BbH - which is realised as a low-rising contour tone. Thus a syllable can carry one of these four melodies H, M, B (>Ba and Bb), BbH. [...] Besides the phonemic units and nasalisation, it is also the tones that serve to differentiate Tepo Krumen signs. Each syllable of a monomorphemic lexeme is characterised by one of the following four melodies: high (H), mid (M), low (B), low-rising (BH)
new_statements.citation: Thalmann, Peter. 2023 (version 230801). Éléments de grammaire kroumen tépo [ted] (parler kru de Côte d'Ivoire). Revised edition of the 1987 Paris 7 thesis. SIL / kroumen-tepo.pbworks.com. 492 pp.
new_statements.locator: §0.3 'Les tons', sommaire (21) and §0.3.1, p. 17 (chapter 0 'Introduction phonologique'); cf. Thalmann 1980 Phonologie du kroumen §3 p. 30
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tepo is a lexical tone language with three levels (high, mid, low; two phonologically distinct low tones Ba and Bb; plus a low-rising BbH sequence); every syllable of every lexeme bears a tone, and the word's prosody is described entirely as tone melodies and tone-change rules. Neither the 1980 phonology nor the 2023 grammar makes any statement about word stress; no fixed or predictable stress position is described.
new_statements.exceptions: Thalmann 2023 §0.1.4 p.14 explains irregular disyllabic tone patterns (tùpǎ 'gibecière', tǔgbà 'clan', hã̌ù 'sauce graine') by 'une pré-association d'un ton à l'une des UPT, due à un phénomène d'accentuation (marquée par *)' — an autosegmental lexical accent (a marked tone-bearing unit), not a stress statement. Words are mostly monosyllabic (about 7/10 nouns, >8/10 verbs); polysyllables are compounds, reduplications or loans (English loans typically B H M).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (lexeme / 'mot phonologique', §0.5); tones cited are inherent tones before tone-change rules; a certain number of realised contours (HB, MB) arise from spreading of Bb within the constituent. Thalmann 1980 §3 p.30 (scanned-corrected): 'Chaque syllabe d'un lexème monomonématique porte un ton. C'est pourquoi le ton peut être considéré comme une prosodie de la syllabe.' Absence of any stress statement was verified by grep of the full text layer (2023) and scanned (1980) for accent/intensité/proéminence/tonique/stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Thalmann's descriptions are of the Tepo dialect proper ('tepo wi', Grabo and Olodio region; informants from Siahé and Gbapé, s/p Grabo), i.e. the core of tepo1239; the 2023 title page misprints the ISO code as [ktj] (Plapo) but the acknowledgements and content give [ted]. Krumen is a continuum: Plapo [ktj] (plap1240) and Piè/Pye [pye] (pyek1239) are separate Glottolog languages treated together in Thalmann's tone papers.

sources.citation: Thalmann, Peter. 2026 (ver3). Tonal puzzles in 3 Krumen languages (SW of Côte d'Ivoire): phonological, grammatical and historical issues. SIL ms. 40 pp.
sources.note: Tone system of Tepo, Plapo, Piè: three levels H/M/L, two low tones La (stable) and Lb (triggers spreading/attraction), LbH rise; tone-change rules and low-tone perfective. Nothing on stress ('accents' = diacritics only).

sources.citation: Thalmann, Peter. 2023 (version 230801, 'à publier prochainement'). Éléments de grammaire kroumen tépo [ted] (parler kru de Côte d'Ivoire). Revised and corrected edition of the 1987 Université de Paris 7 thesis (dir. G. Hérault). 492 pp.
sources.note: Chapter 0 'Introduction phonologique' (pp. 9-46: phonemes, nasalisation, tones §0.3, syllable §0.4, phonological word §0.5, tone rules §0.7). Tepo is a three-level tone language (H, M, B with two low tones Ba/Bb, plus BH); every syllable of a lexeme carries one of four melodies. No statement about word stress / accent d'intensité anywhere; the only 'accent' use (§0.1.4 p.14) is 'un phénomène d'accentuation (marquée par *)' = lexical pre-association of a tone to one TBU in irregular disyllables (tùpǎ 'gibecière', tǔgbà 'clan').
